note: git for-each-ref refs/ns/star matches only ONE COMPONENT DEEP, and git ls-remote does not share that behaviour. This cost a review pass today because the two disagreed and I concluded a ref had been deleted when it never existed in the output. Measured: with refs/hornvale/board and refs/hornvale/peers/ambrose both present, git for-each-ref with pattern refs/hornvale/star prints only refs/hornvale/board, while git show-ref prints both, and git for-each-ref with a TRAILING SLASH prefix refs/hornvale/ prints both. Cause: for-each-ref matches with WM_PATHNAME so star does not cross a slash, whereas ls-remote tail-matches. So a remote query and the equivalent local query can legitimately disagree, and the local one is the liar. Use a trailing-slash prefix, or name the depth explicitly as refs/ns/sub/star, or use git show-ref when you want to see everything. The board tool itself is unaffected because it passes the prefix with the trailing slash already.
